description.value: The study investigated neural representations of a perceptual decision variable and confidence during visual motion discrimination, and tested whether cortical decision-variable signals were linked to confidence signals in the ventral striatum.

spans.text: Here, we used fMRI and multivariate decoding techniques to identify regions of the human brain that encode this decision variable and confidence during a visual motion discrimination task.

Using a multivariate connectivity analysis, we demonstrate that patterns of brain activity in the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex reflecting the decision variable were linked to brain signals in the ventral striatum reflecting confidence.

design.value: An event-related visual motion discrimination fMRI experiment in which participants reported binary motion direction and then rated confidence continuously; analyses included mass-univariate GLM, multivariate searchlight classification, multivariate searchlight regression, and multivariate connectivity.

task_description.value: Participants observed a random dot motion stimulus, reported whether dominant motion was upward or downward, and rated confidence in that judgment.

spans.text: The task of the subject was to observe a random dot motion (RDM) stimulus (Braddick 1974) and then perform two consecutive responses: (1) a binary perceptual judgment of the dominant direction of motion of the stimulus (“motion up” or “motion down”) and (2) a rating of confidence of the judgment on a continuous scale (Fig. 2A).
A trial began by a fixation period of 2, 4, or 6 s (counterbalanced within each experimental run across motion direction and stimulus-response-mapping screen).
All stimuli were created with Matlab (Mathworks) and presented using the Cogent toolbox (http://www.vislab.ucl.ac.uk/Cogent).

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to respond even when they were very unsure.

spans.text: Subjects were instructed to respond even when they were very unsure.

stimuli.value: Random dot motion stimulus with an individually calibrated proportion of dots moving upward or downward and remaining dots moving in random directions.

spans.text: The RDM stimulus was created in a square region of 10 × 10 dva, but only the region within a circular annulus was visible (outer radius: 5 dva, inner radius: 0.85 dva).
The stimulus consisted of 500 dots (5 dots/dva2) that each moved at a speed of 2.5 dva/s and had a diameter of 5.5 arcmin.
Behavioral data of subjects were analyzed for accuracy, response time, and confidence.
